beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — open on the Claude UI, ask shown answered
beats.narration_text: Kia ora, Liam. One Claude prompt. An animated p53 relay — six nodes, one hub, and what breaks when the hub goes dark.

props.command: claude "Port the p53-circuit plate into a Manim scene — 6-node relay, hub node 25% larger, reveal left to right, Flash the hub."

beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — what the six nodes ARE
beats.narration_text: The p53 relay is a six-stage damage-response circuit. A lesion in the DNA triggers sensors — ATM and ATR — that phosphorylate and stabilize p53. p53 then activates effectors: p21 halts the cell cycle at G1; PUMA and Noxa open the apoptosis gate. Six players, a strict left-to-right handoff, and one hub at the centre holding the whole chain together.

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — p53 mutation rate and hub logic
beats.narration_text: TP53 is mutated in roughly fifty percent of all human cancers — the most frequently altered gene in the entire cancer genome. When the hub node fails the relay does not degrade gracefully. Effectors that would have slowed the cell or triggered apoptosis never receive the signal. The chain breaks at node three, and the cell keeps dividing. This is what we want to see move.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — the REAL Claude Code prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The ask,'
beats.narration_text: The ask. Into Claude: port the p53-circuit plate from plates underscore gen dot py into a Manim scene. Geometry: six horizontal nodes, Okabe-Ito colors, hub node index two is twenty-five percent larger. Animation: reveal nodes left to right with LaggedStart, then grow arrows, then Flash the hub to show it is the pivot. Read the command back before you run it — the geometry is in millimetres in SVG space and needs a coordinate transform into Manim's fourteen-wide frame.

props.command:
claude "Port the p53-circuit plate from plates_gen.py into a Manim scene.
Geometry: 6 horizontal nodes, colors [SKY, SKY, BLUE, GREEN, VERM, VERM],
hub node (index 2) is 25% larger. Animate: reveal nodes left->right with
LaggedStart, then grow arrows, then Flash the hub to show it's the pivot."

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_P53Circuit class, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it. The node construction is one list comprehension — RoundedRectangle with the Okabe-Ito fill and a stroke that signals hierarchy: three point two for standard nodes, four point two for the hub. The hub sizing is a single conditional on index two. The choreography is three plays: LaggedStart for the nodes, LaggedStart for the arrows, then a Flash on the hub centre. The Flash is the punctuation — it tells the eye where control lives.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_P53Circuit
props.code:
# scenes.py — Claude Code output
SKY="#56B4E9"; BLUE="#0072B2"; GREEN="#009E73"
VERM="#D55E00"; GRAY="#7c7c7c"
COLS=[SKY,SKY,BLUE,GREEN,VERM,VERM]
XS=[-5.4,-2.7,-0.1,2.5,4.7,6.2]; HUB=2

class B05_P53Circuit(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    config.background_color="#FFFFFF"
    nodes=VGroup(*[
      RoundedRectangle(
        width=2.1*(1.25 if i==HUB else 1.0),
        height=1.15*(1.25 if i==HUB else 1.0),
        corner_radius=0.18,color=COLS[i],
        fill_color=COLS[i],fill_opacity=0.16,
        stroke_width=(4.2 if i==HUB else 3.2)
      ).move_to([xs,0,0]) for i,xs in enumerate(XS)])
    arrows=VGroup(*[Arrow(
      nodes[i].get_right(),nodes[i+1].get_left(),
      buff=0.1,color=GRAY,stroke_width=3.2,
      max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.12
    ) for i in range(5)])
    # choreography
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(n) for n in nodes],
              lag_ratio=0.18,run_time=1.6))
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in arrows],
              lag_ratio=0.14,run_time=1.4))
    self.play(Flash(nodes[HUB].get_center(),color=BLUE,
              line_length=0.4,num_lines=16,flash_radius=1.4),
              nodes[HUB].animate.scale(1.12),run_time=0.5)
    self.play(nodes[HUB].animate.scale(1/1.12),run_time=0.35)
    self.wait(0.8)

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_P53Circuit — watch the LaggedStart reveal and hub Flash
beats.narration_text: Run it. Watch left to right — each node fades in, then its arrow grows before the next node appears. The hub is wider and taller: that is the twenty-five percent scale. When the Flash fires, you see the control point. The pivot of the relay lives at node three. Everything downstream of that Flash depends on what happens at p53.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — revision prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The change,'
beats.narration_text: The change. Revise: stagger the reveal so each arrow grows before the next node appears — one node, then one arrow, then the next node. Then add a collapse sequence after the hub Flash: dim the hub to twenty percent opacity, place an X-mark at its centre, and fade all downstream arrows to fifteen percent. The viewer needs to SEE the circuit break.

props.command:
claude "Revise: stagger reveal so each arrow grows BEFORE the next node appears.
Then add a collapse sequence — hub dims, X-mark appears, arrows through it
fade to 20% opacity — to show the chain breaks when p53 is lost."

beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_P53CircuitBroken — stagger reveal + hub collapse
beats.narration_text: Watch the stagger now: node one in, arrow one grows, node two in, arrow two grows — the relay is telegraphed step by step. Then the Flash, the scale-up, and then the collapse: the hub dims, the X-mark appears in vermillion, and the arrows downstream fade. The circuit does not stop — it just cannot signal. That is the biology. Half of all cancers live in that faded section of the diagram.

beats.role_note: What we built and what the motion taught
beats.narration_text: What did the motion teach? The relay is not a metaphor — it is a clock. Each node fires in sequence and gates the next. The stagger makes that sequencing visible. The collapse makes the consequence visible. Claude ported the SVG geometry into Manim in one prompt and added the collapse scene in one revision. The code is four blocks: node construction, arrow construction, reveal choreography, collapse choreography. Strip that pattern and you can animate any pathway.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: pick any two-node branch off the p53 hub — say, the MDM2 negative feedback loop — and animate it as a separate scene that you can splice after the Flash. Why run it? Because the hub is not actually a one-way relay. MDM2 is a direct p53 target that tags p53 for degradation. The circuit has a feedback arm, and once you animate that arm you can show exactly why p53 accumulates only transiently after damage — and why that transience is intentional.

props.command:
claude "Add a scene: animate the MDM2 negative-feedback arm off the p53 hub.
MDM2 is a p53 target that tags p53 for degradation — show the feedback
arrow looping back, and show how that makes p53 accumulate transiently."
